title: Why do you watch depressing movies?

commenti.body: Bad things are going to happen to you in life. Films (and art) can help you understand and deal with those things and have empathy for others going through hard times. Not to mention appreciating the skills of the actors and filmmakers telling the story.

I just did my 10th (?) viewing of The Man Who Wasn't There, which you might like. It's a Coen film noir, filmed in gorgeous B/W, and it is sad and melancholy, with bits of dark humor. It is a slow-motion disaster affecting everyone connected to the protagonist, unfolding inexorably from one decision. It is accompanied by spare, gorgeous pian renditions of Beethoven's more melancholy compositions.

It's my favorite Coen Bros. movie, and one of my all-time favorites.
I’m not usually a fan of end of the world movies. But melancholia and seeking a friend for the end of the world are so damn good
Meloncholia came to me at the perfect time in my life, I was numb, I feel I truly understood it because of the state I was in, not even the end of the world would phase me at the time.

See I'm different from that kinda view.  I can watch stuff like Requiem for a Dream or Antichrist or Irreversible, etc multiple times.  Or sick and twisted horror stuff.  They're just movies, they don't change how I feel about things.
